subject: Intermittent private-api failures after on‑prem cutover — jump‑host traces attached
messages:
From: Emma Hart <emma.hart@tinyhealth.io>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@tinyhealth.io
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Intermittent 502s to private-api after cutover

Markus —

We flipped our traffic to the private on‑prem cutover last night and started seeing intermittent 502/connection reset errors to the internal private-api (10.240.12.8). Errors are only when requests originate from our app instances in the internal VPC and call the private‑api via the new NAT/gateway path. Publicly-originated requests (via the hosted endpoint) are fine.

Quick facts:
- First observed ~23:10 PST last night after cutover.
- Affects ~25% of requests, sporadic and reproducible on retries.
- We tried curl from one of our app hosts and sometimes get immediate connection reset.
- Traceroute from app host to 10.240.12.8 shows an extra hop (10.200.5.1) that wasn’t present in staging.

I attached a small topology diagram (jumbo-topology.png) and a short pcap capture from the jumphost (jumphost-tcpdump.tgz). Can you advise next steps? We’re blocked for any deployments that hit private-api.

Thanks,
—Emma
Emma Hart
SRE, TinyHealth

Thanks Emma — I can reproduce the traceroute oddity from the artifacts and the pcap looks like we see TCP SYNs, a SYN-ACK, then a RST from the gateway in some flows.

Looping in Dylan (networking) and Vanessa for priority. Dylan — can you take a look at the capture and the extra hop (10.200.5.1)? Hypothesis: MTU/fragmentation + SNAT hairpin or connection tracking timeout causing mid‑handshake resets. Also want to confirm whether security group / firewall is applying asymmetric session policies for internal‑to‑internal routed flows.

Requests:
- Dylan: please pull the pcap and run a quick syn/retrans sequence correlation + tcpdump — interested if the SYN makes it to private-api and whether the gateway is injecting RSTs.
- Emma: can you confirm the app host MTU and whether you enabled jumbo frames for this cluster?
- Vanessa: FYI to coordinate any customer-facing notes or temporary rollback.

Markus

Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 13:42:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent 502s to private-api after cutover

Markus / Vanessa / Emma — I pulled the jumphost pcap from the Drive link (thanks Emma). Quick notes from an initial pass:

1) Handshake pattern: several flows show SYN -> SYN-ACK from 10.240.12.8 -> then immediate RST from 10.200.5.1 (the gateway). The RST originates before the client retransmit which suggests the gateway is either timing out conntrack or deliberately terminating the session.

2) MTU signals: I see a handful of ICMP 'fragmentation needed' messages originating from 10.240.12.8 back to 10.200.5.14 (app edge). The PMTUD path looks inconsistent between app->gateway and gateway->service. If jumbo frames were enabled on the app VPC but not the gateway path that could cause late drops and conntrack state churn.

3) NAT hairpin hypothesis: The gateway uses SNAT for cross‑subnet access; when the service replies it may take a different egress path which hits an ACL that drops reply fragments. That aligns with the asymmetric hop you saw.

Immediate diagnostic asks I executed and included in the trace notes:
- tcpdump filter: "tcp and (host 10.240.12.8 or host 10.200.5.14)"
- correlating TCP sequence numbers to verify whether we see payload that is not being ACKed.

Next steps I recommend:
- Emma: run 'ip link' on an affected app host and paste MTU for the interface and any tun/tap devices.
- Emma: on the jumphost, run 'traceroute -n -M 1400 10.240.12.8' and 'traceroute -n -M 9000 10.240.12.8' to see PMTUD differences.
- Markus: if you can, enable conntrack logging for the gateway short-term to detect timeouts (we can do this with a debug ACL).

I’ll prepare a short playbook for mitigation (force path via non-SNAT peer + temporary MTU clamp).

—Dylan
Senior Network Engineer

Thanks, Dylan — quick answers and outputs below (from an affected app host):

$ ip link show eth0
2: eth0: mtu 9000 qdisc mq state UP mode DEFAULT group default qlen 1000

traceroute -n -M 1400 10.240.12.8
10.200.5.14  1 ms  1 ms  1 ms
10.200.5.1   2 ms  2 ms  2 ms
10.240.12.8   5 ms  5 ms  5 ms

traceroute -n -M 9000 10.240.12.8
10.200.5.14  1 ms  1 ms  1 ms

So our app hosts are on MTU 9000. We did enable jumbo frames for that subnet starting with cutover. We did not touch the gateway MTU. Attached updated pcap and I also uploaded the output to your Drive link.

If we need to roll back the jumbo change on our side I can coordinate — but we’d like guidance for the least-disruptive fix.

Emma
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>

Cc: ops@tinyhealth.io
Date: Thu, 18 Dec 2026 16:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent 502s to private-api after cutover

Update and temporary mitigation:

Dylan confirmed the root cause: MTU mismatch + asymmetric SNAT path produced stray fragments that the gateway did not reassemble before conntrack cleanup, which caused the gateway to RST mid‑handshake for some flows. Two concrete mitigations applied:

1) Temporary MTU clamp on the app‑facing egress rules to 1500 for the TinyHealth subnet (applied 2026-12-18T14:20:00-08:00). This eliminates PMTUD fragmentation on the path.
2) We added a deterministic SNAT exception rule so that internal app→private-api flows keep symmetric source IPs while we rollout full gateway jumbo support.

Post‑mitigation checks (14:40–15:50 PST):
- Error rates dropped from 25%→<1% on TinyHealth traffic.
- No further RST injection observed in the jumphost tcpdumps.

Action items:
- TinyHealth: plan a maintenance window so we can coordinate enabling jumbo frames end‑to‑end (gateway + intermediate devices).
- Redwood: schedule a configuration rollout to remove the temp SNAT exception once heterogeneous MTU is resolved (JIRA NET-4128).

Vanessa: please coordinate a short customer note and close the escalation once TinyHealth confirms full stability.

Thanks team — Markus
